column1:
Cyclical signals in the May 3, 2017 FOMC statement are mildly constructive—solid job gains, firming business investment, and a transitory view of the Q1 growth slowdown—while inflation is still somewhat below 2 percent and policy remains accommodative with a gradual, data‑dependent path.

Overlaying the Financial Stability Report perspective tempers that optimism: financial conditions are easy and risk appetite is elevated, with stretched asset valuations and higher nonfinancial corporate leverage. At the same time, household balance sheets and bank capital/liquidity are solid and funding risks remain low. This mix supports the Committee’s gradualism but warrants added caution about potential vulnerability to an abrupt repricing.

Net effect: still positive but a bit more guarded than before.
